title: The New Song of the New Creation
english: Those who were far from God have been persuaded to worship, and they will be called through the faith that is in Christ. They will come to know the King and Lord of all things, and the word shows this very clearly in prophecy.

For he commands those who have received mercy through God to glorify him, saying: Sing to the Lord a new song; let the beginning of it be praise, and glorify his name from the farthest corners of the earth—those who go down to the sea and sail upon it, the islands and all who dwell on them.

This song is new, and it befits the newness of the things that have come to be. For if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation; as it is written, the old things have passed away, and behold, all things have become new.

Indeed, the children of Israel were ransomed from the greed of Egypt, with the wise Moses mediating at that time. They were freed from brick-making, from the empty sweat of earthly labors, from the harsh toil imposed by taskmasters, and from the inhumanity of their rulers.
They were led through the midst of the sea, ate manna in the wilderness, drank water from the rock, crossed the Jordan on dry ground, and were brought into the land of promise.
All these things are now new for us, and the old things are incomparably surpassed by what is better.
We have been set apart not for fleshly service, but for spiritual service; we have been separated from the earthly labors that arise from fleshly affection and from their pollutions.

We did not flee merely Egyptian overseers, nor even a tyrant who was impious and savage, except as a man among us. Rather, we have been turned away from those who urge us toward sin—wicked and unclean demons—and from the one who stands over their herds, that is, Satan.

We crossed through as if over a certain sea — the surge of this present life, its inner turmoil, and the truly burdensome distractions that pull us in every direction. We ate the intellectual manna, the bread that comes down from heaven, the very life given to the world. We drank water from the rock, having delighted in the spiritual gifts of Christ, which are clearly known to the intellect.

We crossed the Jordan, having been deemed worthy of the holy baptism, and entered into the land promised and fitting for the saints — a land which the Savior himself mentions, saying, 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.' Therefore, in light of these new beginnings, it was necessary that a new hymn arise from its very source: from those who have come into being through him and who now begin their life in him. This hymn must be his fitting praise, not confined merely to the land of Judah, but proclaimed indeed from the farthest end of the earth to the other end, clearly encompassing all that is under heaven. For formerly, God was known only in Judah, and his name was great in Israel alone. But now, since we have been called through Christ to the full knowledge of truth, that knowledge has become complete.

title: Heedful Listening
english: The people of Israel have a unique relationship with God, which has been clearly stated, so that it may be evident that God is involved in everything.
It was necessary for those who honored ungodliness toward God to be excluded from his care and love.

However, those who were held captive by sin due to ignorance and had fallen under the devil's control were to be killed by the creator of all, and yet they were called to know him and to experience the light of truth.

This is also evident in the words of the all-wise Moses, who said that the people provoked God to jealousy with idols and angered him with their pursuits, as he stated: 'They provoked me to jealousy with those who are not gods, they angered me with their idols; and I will provoke them to jealousy with a nation that is not a nation; with a foolish nation I will anger them' (Deuteronomy 32:21).

The prophetic Melitos also stated that the people provoked God with their idols and pursuits, and as a result, God saw their actions, despised them, and greatly humbled Israel, for it is written: 'They provoked him with their idols and with their pursuits, and the Lord God saw and despised and greatly humbled Israel'.

Nevertheless, if we are to interpret these words spiritually, we must be cautious not to fall into the devil's trap in our minds and hearts, and not to be swayed by the evil idols in our fantasies that call us to licentiousness and perverse pleasures, lest we become prey to Satan and demons.

It is essential to pay attention to the words of Scripture, for they offer a remedy for great sins, as it is written: 'If the spirit of the one in authority rises up against you, do not leave your place, because a remedy will calm great sins' (Proverbs 24:19).
Who among you pays attention to these things? Listen to what is coming.

The divinely inspired writer encourages us to listen carefully, so that we may receive the word with a clear mind and store it in our heart, as the psalmist says: 'I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you' (Psalm 119:11).
This is also evident in the 48th psalm, where it is written: 'Hear this, all nations; give ear, all inhabitants of the world' (Psalm 48:1).

Hearing is common to all who have once perceived a sound or some other noise, but paying attention is to bring something of the established things into one's mind, and to store it in both mind and heart.

The prophetic word seeks those who have listened more gently and thoughtfully, so that they may speak about the safety of future things based on past events, as Paul says: 'These things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our instruction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come' (1 Corinthians 10:11).

We must not encounter the stories about him in vain, but rather receive them for the benefit of our soul, and avoid being caught in the same sins, so that we may not fall into the same disasters as they did.

title: Perseverance of the Saints
english: The Lord says that the one once chosen by his hands will not be taken away, for the one from his hands is not removed, as he says, 'I will do, and who will turn it back?' He has made the calling of the nations, or, in other words, he has saved those who were being led astray, and now he asks, 'Who will change this, that is, change it to not be so?' For, as the Savior himself says, no one will snatch the ones saved by him from the hand of God (John 10:28-29).

My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; I give them eternal life, and they will not perish, and no one will snatch them from my hand; my Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them from the hand of my Father (John 10:27-29). The Lord God, who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel, says, 'I will send to Babylon for your sake, and I will stir up all the fugitives, and the Chaldeans will be bound in ships' (Isaiah 43:14).

Through the things recently said, a strong exhortation has been given to those called from the nations to knowledge of him, and it has been shown that he alone has knowledge of the beginning, middle, and end, and that there is no other who can save completely; he is all-powerful, a wonder-worker, and the natures of things obey his nods, with the elements of the world serving him, and whatever he wills is certainly accomplished, with nothing lying at his feet to hinder him.

The Israelites, having slipped into idolatry and disobedience, needed much guidance and stability of mind, as well as much light and exhortations and reminders; God, in his power and glory, makes known to them the future and reveals the disasters that will befall the Babylonians, showing that they will be taken captive, and through this, the Israelites will be convinced that the shameful things of all are proclaimed through them, as I said.

As the discussion turns to great matters, God necessarily shows the incomparable glory of his power, saying, 'Thus says the Lord God, who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel' (Isaiah 43:14); for God wants to remind them of the past, of the redemption from Egypt, when a great multitude of miracles testified to him …
